signal.summary: Xiaomi released MiMo V2.6 Pro and Flash with tool use, long context and open RL task environments.

candidates.title: Capability Gap Closure Compiler
candidates.hypothesis: Translate a detected missing UberBond capability into hundreds of bounded implementation, test, benchmark and integration microtasks that cheap workers can execute in parallel.
candidates.mechanism: Frontier models specify the missing capability and acceptance contract; JEV/local workers fan it into dependency-aware microtasks and compile repeated successful paths into deterministic code.
candidates.falsifier: On held-out capability gaps, accepted completion rate or founder-minute savings fails to improve over the current implementation workflow.
candidates.nextProbe: Shadow-run on three recent missing-capability tasks and compare accepted completion, retries, cost and founder minutes.

candidates.title: Million-Microtask Factory
candidates.hypothesis: Large frontier-authored missions can be converted into very large populations of tiny verifiable jobs without proportionally increasing frontier-token use.
candidates.mechanism: A typed task compiler emits idempotent jobs with evidence contracts, allowing local and cheap-cloud workers to execute only minimum-sufficient context.
candidates.falsifier: Total mission cost or defect rate grows linearly with microtask count and shows no advantage over monolithic execution.
candidates.nextProbe: Compile one repo mission into 1,000 synthetic zero-effect tasks and measure orchestration overhead and verification quality.

candidates.title: Cross-Model Serendipity Market
candidates.hypothesis: Unexpectedly useful ideas can be found by deliberately crossing outputs from models that disagree or specialize differently.
candidates.mechanism: A broker pairs distant candidate concepts from frontier, MiMo and local-model outputs, then tests only combinations with measurable complementarity.
candidates.falsifier: Cross-model recombination yields no higher novelty-adjusted testability than same-model recombination on a blinded sample.
candidates.nextProbe: Generate 100 pairings from heterogeneous and homogeneous pools and blind-score novelty, feasibility and downstream testability.

candidates.title: Autonomous Model-Release Assimilator
candidates.hypothesis: A major model release can automatically create new capability hypotheses, benchmarks, routing experiments and implementation candidates without redesigning UberBond.
candidates.mechanism: Gamechanger evidence triggers GENESIS, Capability Genome deltas, a model tournament and candidate downstream architecture mutations under zero-effect gates.
candidates.falsifier: A release produces no actionable capability delta or the generated experiments fail to distinguish the new model from incumbents.
candidates.nextProbe: Use MiMo-V2.6 as the first replay and compare generated capability deltas against a manual expert review.

candidates.title: Hypothesis-to-Replication Conveyor
candidates.hypothesis: Scientific hypotheses can be compiled directly into reproducible computational experiments and replication packets.
candidates.mechanism: A science actuator maps claim, falsifier and evidence requirements into simulation, code, datasets, controls and independent replay steps.
candidates.falsifier: Independent replay cannot reproduce results or the compiler systematically omits necessary controls.
candidates.nextProbe: Compile five repository-safe computational hypotheses into double-blind replay packets and measure reproducibility.

candidates.title: Research-to-Tool Fabricator
candidates.hypothesis: When a research paper reveals a useful mechanism, UberBond can automatically create a bounded instrument that tests that mechanism against its own workloads.
candidates.mechanism: A paper-to-instrument pipeline extracts mechanism, implementation constraints, license boundaries and a falsifiable local benchmark before any promotion.
candidates.falsifier: Generated tools fail the benchmark or cannot preserve provenance/license boundaries better than manual implementation.
candidates.nextProbe: Select three open research mechanisms and attempt clean-room bounded instrument builds with exact evidence lineage.

candidates.title: Scientific Forgetting Engine
candidates.hypothesis: UberBond can improve discovery by actively retiring stale assumptions, duplicated hypotheses and obsolete experiment paths while preserving their lineage.
candidates.mechanism: A decay engine tracks prediction failures, superseding evidence and dependency use, archiving low-value scientific beliefs without deleting provenance.
candidates.falsifier: Archive decisions remove a belief later required for a successful prediction more often than a conservative baseline.
candidates.nextProbe: Replay historical hypothesis evolution and measure false-retirement rate before enabling any automatic archive proposals.

candidates.title: Stale-Theory Garbage Collector
candidates.hypothesis: Repeated failed predictions can be converted into explicit pressure against theories that continue consuming search budget.
candidates.mechanism: Prediction receipts update theory utility and divert compute toward alternatives when a falsification threshold is crossed.
candidates.falsifier: Compute reallocation reduces discovery quality or retires theories before sufficient evidence exists.
candidates.nextProbe: Simulate theory portfolios with known ground truth and compare conservative versus aggressive retirement thresholds.

candidates.title: Model Labor Exchange
candidates.hypothesis: Models and local compute cells can compete for typed cognitive jobs as suppliers in an internal market rather than being statically assigned.
candidates.mechanism: Each task publishes capability, privacy, latency, cost and evidence requirements; suppliers bid with measured fitness and the router chooses the minimum sufficient bundle.
candidates.falsifier: Market routing costs more or performs worse than a fixed best-model policy across a held-out workload.
candidates.nextProbe: Run a shadow exchange over recorded tasks using measured model prices, latency and acceptance outcomes.

candidates.title: Capability Futures Market
candidates.hypothesis: UberBond can allocate research attention using internal prediction markets on which emerging capabilities will become valuable.
candidates.mechanism: Agents submit calibrated probability and value estimates tied to falsifiable future observations; scoring rewards calibration rather than confidence.
candidates.falsifier: The market fails to outperform simple equal-weight forecasting on Brier score and realized utility ranking.
candidates.nextProbe: Backtest on historical model/tool releases with time-sliced evidence and compare against simple baselines.

candidates.title: Agent Instrument Forge
candidates.hypothesis: GENESIS can invent new measurement tools when existing metrics cannot discriminate between candidate agent architectures.
candidates.mechanism: A meta-instrument generator derives observable variables from the competing hypotheses, creates probes and validates measurement reliability before use.
candidates.falsifier: Invented instruments have low test-retest reliability or do not change architecture selection compared with existing metrics.
candidates.nextProbe: Choose three ambiguous agent comparisons and generate candidate instruments, then measure reliability and decision value.

candidates.title: Autonomous Benchmark Synthesizer
candidates.hypothesis: UberBond can generate fresh anti-gaming benchmarks from real failure traces instead of relying only on static public suites.
candidates.mechanism: Failure receipts are transformed into minimal reproducible tasks with hidden variants, contamination checks and independent scoring.
candidates.falsifier: Generated benchmarks correlate poorly with real production failures or are easily overfit by candidate models.
candidates.nextProbe: Create a hidden benchmark from 20 historical repo defects and compare model rankings with subsequent real-task performance.

candidates.title: Personal Research Frontier Compiler
candidates.hypothesis: The discovery engine can prioritize research paths by how much they expand Mohamed's reachable future options without hard-coding one life trajectory.
candidates.mechanism: Candidate research programs are scored on option creation, reversibility, learning value and evidence, with human choice retained at commitment points.
candidates.falsifier: The ranking fails to identify higher-option outcomes on retrospective blinded cases or becomes unstable to small preference changes.
candidates.nextProbe: Run only on explicit non-sensitive preference dimensions and compare against equal-weight and novelty-only baselines.

candidates.title: Founder-Curiosity Telescope
candidates.hypothesis: UberBond can surface distant but potentially transformative research directions that would not appear in ordinary goal-directed search.
candidates.mechanism: A bounded curiosity budget samples low-similarity areas, maps them to current capability gaps and requires a falsifiable reason for retaining each branch.
candidates.falsifier: Low-similarity sampling produces no more high-value survivors than random exploration after controlling for review budget.
candidates.nextProbe: Compare structured distant-search, random-search and nearest-neighbor search over the same evaluation budget.

candidates.title: Capability Chimera Compiler
candidates.hypothesis: Existing small capabilities can be recombined into novel higher-order tools before building or buying a new monolithic capability.
candidates.mechanism: A compatibility graph searches compositions, simulates permissions and dependencies, then benchmarks the minimum sufficient bundle.
candidates.falsifier: Composed bundles are less reliable or more expensive than single-purpose incumbent tools across matched tasks.
candidates.nextProbe: Search the current capability graph for ten unmet tasks and tournament compositions against incumbent routes.

candidates.title: Missing-Organ Auto-Builder
candidates.hypothesis: When the 890-tree identifies a shared missing ancestor, UberBond can propose and build the smallest reusable internal primitive that unlocks the largest downstream region.
candidates.mechanism: Technology-tree leverage scores feed a primitive synthesizer; generated code must pass provenance, security, hostile tests and exact downstream callability checks.
candidates.falsifier: Built primitives do not unlock predicted descendants or increase maintenance burden more than their measured reuse value.
candidates.nextProbe: Select the highest-leverage internal ancestor blocker and build one zero-external-effect prototype under a throwaway branch.

candidates.title: Possibility Yield Metric
candidates.hypothesis: Compute allocation can be optimized for verified increase in reachable options rather than raw token throughput.
candidates.mechanism: A metric combines validated capability gain, uncertainty reduction, reversibility and downstream dependency unlocks per unit compute.
candidates.falsifier: The metric has no predictive relationship with later accepted capability gains and performs no better than cost or token count alone.
candidates.nextProbe: Backtest candidate formulas against historical accepted/rejected UberBond changes and preregister a prospective version.

candidates.title: Discovery Joules Ledger
candidates.hypothesis: Local scientific and ideation workloads can be compared by verified discovery progress per measured joule rather than energy-equivalent token estimates.
candidates.mechanism: UberWatt measured kWh is joined with accepted hypothesis, benchmark and capability outcomes to compute an evidence-bound discovery-energy ratio.
candidates.falsifier: Outcome attribution is too noisy or the metric rewards trivial micro-results instead of meaningful discovery.
candidates.nextProbe: Instrument one local worker with external energy measurement and compare several task classes without changing household electrical hardware.

candidates.title: Counterfactual Founder Twin
candidates.hypothesis: A bounded digital twin can simulate decision consequences without being granted authority to choose on Mohamed's behalf.
candidates.mechanism: The twin holds explicit assumptions and uncertainty distributions, runs counterfactual branches and exposes sensitivity to preference changes.
candidates.falsifier: Its forecasts are poorly calibrated on outcomes with available retrospective data or recommendations change wildly under tiny assumption perturbations.
candidates.nextProbe: Build a sandbox twin from explicitly supplied non-sensitive variables and score calibration on historical reversible decisions.

candidates.title: Decision Doppelganger Laboratory
candidates.hypothesis: Multiple alternative decision models can compete as transparent simulated advisers rather than collapsing uncertainty into one recommendation.
candidates.mechanism: Each adviser embodies a declared objective/assumption set; disagreements trigger evidence collection instead of forced consensus.
candidates.falsifier: Ensembling does not improve calibration or exposes no useful disagreement compared with a single baseline model.
candidates.nextProbe: Create three transparent advisers for one reversible low-stakes planning problem and score forecast diversity and calibration.

candidates.title: Autonomy Compression Ratio
candidates.hypothesis: UberBond can measure how much frontier reasoning has been safely compiled downward into deterministic or cheap cognition.
candidates.mechanism: Track accepted task-equivalent work completed by deterministic/JEV/local layers versus frontier calls, weighted by quality and exception rate.
candidates.falsifier: The ratio rises while defect rate or hidden frontier intervention also rises, showing the metric is gameable.
candidates.nextProbe: Replay a fixed task suite while progressively compiling repeated decisions and measure quality-adjusted frontier-token displacement.

candidates.title: Verified Progress Exchange Rate
candidates.hypothesis: Every compute supplier can be priced in a common unit of accepted verified progress per dollar, kWh and founder minute.
candidates.mechanism: Normalize task outcomes into evidence-backed acceptance units and estimate marginal progress rates for local models, APIs and deterministic code.
candidates.falsifier: The common unit fails stability tests across task classes or induces routing choices that lower real acceptance.
candidates.nextProbe: Construct a held-out mixed workload and compare routing by progress exchange rate against token-cost and intelligence-score baselines.

candidates.title: Centennial Option Preserver
candidates.hypothesis: Long-horizon technology choices can be screened for irreversible lock-in that destroys future capability paths.
candidates.mechanism: A horizon scanner maps dependencies, switching costs and option loss, then adds an explicit reversibility penalty before major architecture commitments.
candidates.falsifier: The penalty consistently blocks beneficial commitments without predicting meaningful future lock-in risk.
candidates.nextProbe: Backtest on historical technology choices with known migration outcomes and compare against cost-only selection.

candidates.title: Future-Ancestor Research Portfolio
candidates.hypothesis: Research can be selected partly by the number and diversity of future capabilities it could become an ancestor of.
candidates.mechanism: Technology-tree simulations estimate downstream descendant unlocks under uncertainty, while a portfolio constraint prevents one speculative lineage from consuming the budget.
candidates.falsifier: Predicted ancestor leverage does not correlate with later realized descendant reuse or crowds out nearer evidence-backed work.
candidates.nextProbe: Backtest ancestor-leverage scores on existing UberBond primitives and then run a small shadow allocation portfolio.

truthBoundary: THIS NURSERY CONTAINS GENERATED HYPOTHESES WITH FALSIFIERS AND PROBES. IT IS NOT PROOF OF DISCOVERY, FEASIBILITY, IMPLEMENTATION, MARKET VALUE OR EXTERNAL EFFECT.
